visual.general_description: Three unlettered external-device photographs demonstrate the AttachBend control and two bending orientations.
visual.detailed_description: A large left handle photograph and two stacked right distal-shaft photographs are separated by black borders. No panel letters are printed, so the composite is recorded as a single whole-figure panel. The upper-right view carries a 70° overlay and up-angulation text; the lower-right view carries down-angulation text.

panels.general_description: Composite of three device photographs (no printed panel letters): the AttachBend control on an endoscope handle and the distal shaft bent in two attachment orientations.
panels.detailed_description: Unlettered three-view composite separated by thick black borders. The large left view shows a purple-gloved hand holding a black therapeutic endoscope handle with rotary controls; a white circular attachment control near the lower handle carries FUJIFILM branding and a curved scale marked 0° and 70°, with a black-and-silver shaft lying diagonally on a pale background. The upper-right view shows a horizontal black shaft with a silver articulated segment bending upward to a curled black tip, white reference lines with an angular arc labelled 70°, and yellow text 'attached in the up-angulation direction'. The lower-right view shows the articulated segment bending downward to a hooked black tip with yellow text 'attached in the down-angulation direction'. No panel letters, rulers or patient tissue appear.

imaging_modalities.visual_cue: External photographs show an endoscope/attachment on a plain surface, not an in-body medical acquisition.

evidence.quote: We report a successful ESD utilizing this device for management of lesions in the greater curvature of the lower gastric body (Video 1).

pixel_observations: Left view: purple-gloved fingers grip the black endoscope handle; a white circular external control with a 0°-70° scale sits near the lower handle.

Lower-right view: articulated segment bends downward, distal tip curls back, yellow down-angulation text.

evidence.quote:
Fig. 1.
AttachBend (Fujifilm) is an external attachment device designed to provide an additional bending point to the distal portion of a therapeutic endoscope, with a maximum angulation of 70°. The image on the left displays the control lever of the device mounted on the endoscope handle. The upper-right image demonstrates the configuration when the device is attached in the up-angulation direction, whereas the lower-right image demonstrates the attachment in the down-angulation direction.
